title: US EPA Chemistry Data Sharing Platforms for the Community | Antony Williams
description:
At the recent American Chemical Society meeting in Chicago I gave three talks. This is the second of three of the talks "US EPA Chemistry Data Sharing Platforms for the Community"

In the past ten years the US-EPA has delivered a number of data sharing web-based tools using chemistry data as the foundation. These include the CompTox Chemicals Dashboard, the Cheminformatics Modules, AMOS, the Analytical Methods and Open Spectra database and CheT, the Chemical Transformations database. The underlying chemistry data have been registered and curated in the DSSTox database for over three decades and integrated with other data to deliver to the community. The CompTox Chemicals Dashboard provides access to experimental and predicted physicochemical properties and fate and transport data, in vivo and in vitro toxicity data, exposure data and a number of flexible searches to access the data. The Cheminformatics Modules (CIM) is a suite of tools allowing for hazard and safety profiling of chemical substances, real time QSAR prediction of property and toxicity endpoints and includes AMOS, a document centric system mapping over half a million documents to tens of thousands of chemical substances. The documents include chemical fact sheets, analytical methods, product declaration and safety data sheets, and include, in the integrated system, linkage to over 2.8 million spectra. CIM also includes CheT, the Chemical Transformations Database providing access to thousands of chemicals and their associated transformation product reaction pathways. This suite of software applications supports various needs across the EPA and the public and this presentation will provide an overview of the history of their development, capabilities and how they are used by various offices across the agency to support for example, risk assessment and emergency response scenarios. This abstract does not necessarily represent the views or policies of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

title: Delivering Integrated Chemical Transformation Data for Pesticides via Web-Based Tools | Antony Williams
description:
At the recent American Chemical Society meeting in Chicago I gave three talks. This is the third of three of the talks "Delivering Integrated Chemical Transformation Data for Pesticides via Web-Based Tools".

Pesticides breakdown in the environment via complex reaction pathways, many of which have been documented in historical reports but not easily accessible in terms of searching. The US-EPA has built a suite of web-based tools to provide access to chemistry-related data and providing the ability to perform hazard profiling, physicochemical property and fate and transport endpoint modeling and searching across tens of thousands of documents. Two of these modules in particular deliver insight into detailed information regarding pesticides and their associated environmental transformations. AMOS, the Analytical Methods and Open Spectral database and CheT, the Chemical Transformations database, link together thousands of transformations from the original documented source to a structured database of pathways. This presentation will deliver an overview of both applications and how they continue to expand to provide access to data regarding the environmental fate of chemicals with a specific focus on pesticide-related datasets. This abstract does not necessarily represent the views or policies of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

title: Building dense or compact cities without jeopardizing biodiversity: Insights from bird observations in Gothenburg, Sweden - npj Urban Sustainability
description: A central challenge for sustainable urban development is balancing the trade-offs of high urban density. We examined whether biodiversity can be supported within dense or compact urban areas by analyzing bird species richness and composition across 30 sites in Gothenburg, Sweden, representing three urban form types (two compact and one dense) and reference areas with abundant vegetation. Results showed that species richness was significantly lower in the three urban form types than in the reference areas, and species composition differed significantly between the two groups. However, there were no significant differences in species richness or composition between the individual urban form types themselves. Across the three urban form types, nevertheless, sites with larger local natural habitat area and/or better connectivity to surrounding natural habitats had higher species richness, whereas variation in species composition was associated primarily with local habitat area. This highlights that increasing habitat area remains the most effective strategy for supporting avian diversity, even in dense or compact urban areas. Species that are less common in urban areas were also recorded at sites within the three urban form types where suitable conditions existed. These results not only suggest that biodiversity can exist within dense or compact urban areas but also that it can be supported through both site-level interventions and broader-scale planning for habitat connectivity.

title: Supporting America's Ranchers
description: By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: Section 1.  Policy. Every child deserves a safe and nurturing home where they can learn, grow, and reach their full potential. Adoption makes that possible by opening the door to stability and belonging for children who need a family. During National Adoption Month, we commend the parents whose love has changed lives and the children whose presence has completed families -- and we recommit to caring for the many children still waiting for the comfort and security of a permanent home.Adoption reflects the deep value our Nation places on family and abundant life. As President, I am committed to empowering families who answer the call to open their hearts and homes to children. Through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, I made the adoption tax credit more accessible and expanded the child tax credit, helping remove financial barriers to adopting and allowing families to save more of their income to care for their children. While adoption creates beautiful new beginnings, too many children in our foster care system still wait for a permanent home. During my first term, I took monumental action to strengthen America's foster care and adoption systems by signing into law the landmark Family First Prevention Services Act -- the most sweeping reform of Federal child welfare policy in decades. This law utilizes proven intervention methods to keep families intact and prevent unnecessary separation. This term, I remain firmly committed to continuing this vital work alongside First Lady Melania Trump. Just last week, I signed an Executive Order on Fostering the Future for American Children and Families, to harness Federal support, technology, and strategic partnerships to provide young Americans in, or transitioning out of, the foster-care system with the tools they need to become successful adults. This effort is strengthened by the leadership of the First Lady whose work continues to uplift and protect the well-being of America's children -- ensuring every child has greater access to a strong foundation for the future. This month, we recognize the profound truth that all children are a gift from God, worthy of love, care, and family. We honor the parents and families who welcome children into their homes and provide the stability and guidance every young person deserves. Above all, we commit to protecting children, supporting those who care for them, and strengthening the pillar of family across our great Nation. NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do hereby proclaim November 2025 as National Adoption Month throughout the United States. I encourage all Americans to observe this month by supporting children in need of a safe and loving home, uplifting the families who welcome them, and helping strengthen the bonds of family and community across our Nation.
